challenges.title: Pack and unpack a CAN message with CRC and alive counter
challenges.prompt: Implement crc8, encode and decode for a sensor message: a signed 0.1 C temperature, an rpm value, a 4-bit alive counter and a CRC-8 in byte 7. Decode must reject corrupted frames and wrong counters. This runs on your computer as ordinary C; it models the signal packing you would do on an S32K node, but uses no hardware.
challenges.expected:
83 FF B8 0B 0F 00 00 56 
decode: 0 temp=-12.5 rpm=3000 ctr=15
wrong counter: -2
corrupted: -1
challenges.explain: Little-endian signals are assembled byte by byte, the counter uses the low nibble, and the CRC covers bytes 0 to 6. Decode checks the CRC before trusting any field, then the counter. Verified by compiling and running with gcc on the host.

challenges.title: A UDS request handler
challenges.prompt: Implement respond for services 0x10, 0x22 and 0x3E with the specified negative response codes, including a DID that is only readable in the extended session. This is a host-side model of the service logic; real UDS also needs ISO-TP transport, timing (P2) and security access.
challenges.expected:
read VIN       -> 62 F1 90 56 49 4E
read 0100 dflt -> 7F 22 7F
ext session    -> 50 03 00 32 01 F4
read 0100 ext  -> 62 01 00 2A
bad subfunc    -> 7F 10 12
tester present -> 7E 00
short read     -> 7F 22 13
unknown DID    -> 7F 22 31
unknown svc    -> 7F 85 11
challenges.explain: Validate length first, then sub-function or identifier, then session state, returning 7F SID NRC on failure. Positive responses add 0x40 to the service ID. Verified by compiling and running with gcc on the host; no ECU or CAN hardware was used.
